And I think of the Southern Cross-Country Championship at Brighton in 1930, when we were placed in this event for the first time, led by smiling Syd.

Harry Verney was soon found a job when he visited us, and he looked as if he was enjoying the sound of shoes on mud again. Syd Warboys has moved from Essex to Wallasey, Cheshire. Mick Walker is now convalescing from an attack of pleurisy.

We hope that he will be able to visit us occasionally, and we look forward to seeing his genial person. Syd. Warboys writes from Wallasey, Cheshire, and keeps fit by evening walks by the sea and week-ends in North Wales.
Our past performances in this race were not noticeable until 1930, when we secured our first placing, our team being third and the scoring men were: S.
Our team and their scoring positions was: A. Allum 4, S.
Our star runners were Allum, who did fastest time over his stretch and Syd Warboys, running for the first time who was second fastest on the long fifth stage of those days of 6 miles 352 yards.

Sid Warboys … pegged back Hallamshire and Surrey AC and handed over fifth. Joe Flower carried on the good work, overhauling Highgate and Tipton and bringing us up to third.
The race had reached “The Feathers” at Merstham and we were within three seconds of the medals. Stage five ended at “The Chequers,” Horley, by which time Syd Warboys had had to give way to Aldershot.
